Lighthouse 93/100/100/100 (accessibility/best-practices/seo all still perfect; performance sub-score driven by first-contentful-paint 0.65/largest-contentful-paint 0.88, both ~2.6s - the same shared-shell bfcache-blocked and unused-CSS pattern already flagged in prior testing-pillar design reviews as owner:integrator, not this article's markup; 5 concurrent node.exe processes were observed on the machine during this run, so the FCP number may be somewhat pessimistic from contention rather than a regression). Screenshots read: all 16 desktop-light parts (full article, start to footer), all 22 mobile-dark parts (full article, start to footer), desktop-dark fold+part01 (diagram)+part06 (spare red-step)+part08 (strike/ArgumentOutOfRangeException red-step), mobile-light fold+part02 (diagram)+part10 (strike/ArgumentOutOfRangeException red-step)+part16 (perfect-game-shortcut/ArgumentOutOfRangeException red-step). Every one of the article's red-step failure panels was inspected on at least one width/theme, and the two ArgumentOutOfRangeException crash panels and the CS0246 compile-error panel were each checked in more than one theme/width combination.
justification: This is a well-built, disciplined long-form kata walkthrough that clears the design bar. The single diagram (Figure 1, the red-green-refactor loop) is correctly built to spec: a 300-wide portrait stack well under the 360 budget, so it never scrolls at 390px in either theme, 12-14 unit text stays crisp at both widths, and the three semantic box colors (d-box-bad/d-box-good/d-box-accent) read clearly in both light and dark without becoming a small stranded island on desktop. The figcaption stands alone without depending on anything scrolled off-screen. Heading hierarchy is clean (only ## used for every section, no ### at all, matching the 'On this page' nav one-to-one with h1=1). Both exercises are correctly collapsed (closed 'Show solution' triangle) in every theme/width screenshot checked, including the second exercise's fairly long nested code-block solution. The repeated red/green/refactor cadence across five laps is the article's biggest design risk, and it avoids monotony deliberately rather than by accident: Lap 1's red step is a compiler error (CS0246) rather than a failed assertion, the 'checkpoint' section is a green-first-try with no new code (a genuine break in the pattern), a bonus 'bowling-shortcut' block demonstrates a regression the checkpoint's test alone catches, and the refactor lap has no red step at all. The two exercises sit at natural pauses (end of Lap 3, end of the closing discussion) rather than being bolted on. Compared against two real, well-known bowling-kata walkthroughs (Ron Jeffries' original C# version and Uncle Bob's kata write-up), both of which are static prose with no dark theme, no phone-specific layout, no diagram, and no collapsible exercises, this article is substantially more illustrated and interactive while covering the same ground with real, verified tool output rather than hand-typed listings. The one recurring weak point: the two ArgumentOutOfRangeException crash panels (Lap 4's red step and the 'bowling-shortcut' regression demo) both show the exception type but scroll off the explanatory 'Index was out of range...' message and the full failing-test name past the visible ~40-column mobile window, in both light and dark - see issue below. It is a real, repeated pattern (the exact case the assignment asked to check carefully) but it does not break the article's argument, since the surrounding prose never quotes the clipped message text and the pass/fail fact plus exception type are both visible before the fade.

issues.location: Lap 4 red-step output panel ('This is not a wrong number to fix...', id=bowling-v4-red) and the 'bowling-shortcut' red-step output panel in 'A checkpoint that needed no new code'; seen clipped in mobile-dark part10/part16 and mobile-light part10/part16, and even on desktop (desktop-dark part08, desktop-light part08) where the box is much wider than the message
issues.problem: Both panels print the real xUnit.net v3 line `System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException : Index was out of range. Must be non-negative and less than the size of the collection. (Parameter 'index')`, and on every width checked the panel's fixed-width box shows only `System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException` before the line is scrolled off; the actual explanatory message ('Index was out of range...') is never visible without manually scrolling, on desktop as well as mobile, since the line is simply longer than the panel is wide. The `GameTests.StrikeThenThreeFour_ScoresTwentyFour [FAIL]` / `GameTests.AllStrikes_ScoresThreeHundred [FAIL]` test-name lines above them are also cut mid-identifier on mobile. The prose does not quote the clipped message text, so the pass/fail fact and the exception type both survive, but a reader relying on the panel alone cannot see why the exception happened from the panel itself.
issues.fixLooksLike: Not really fixable without altering real captured output, which the article correctly refuses to fake, and this is genuinely how .NET renders that exception's Message. Worth a note for the technical critic on whether a shorter parameter/variable name upstream would shorten the message, but most likely accept as-is: it matches the same class of minor, real-output clipping already accepted in docs/reviews/testing/unit-testing-fundamentals.round-1.design.json; not blocking.

issues.problem: Performance is 93, which clears the >=90 gate but is meaningfully lower than the 99 seen on sibling testing-pillar articles; first-contentful-paint scores only 0.65 (2.6s). The same shared-shell sub-audits already flagged elsewhere are present here too: 'Page prevented back/forward cache restoration' scores 0, and 'Reduce unused CSS' scores 0.5. Separately, the front matter's `prerequisites: ["testing/unit-testing-fundamentals"]` does not currently render a 'Before you read' box on the page, because src/content/articles/testing/unit-testing-fundamentals.md does not yet exist on this branch (only test-doubles.md and test-driven-development.md are present under src/content/articles/testing/ here) - this is expected per WRITER_GUIDE.md ('shown once published') and self-resolves once the two branches merge, not a defect in this article.
issues.fixLooksLike: Re-run verify-page serially with no other worktree builds running to get a clean performance number before the final gate; if it stays materially below 99, investigate FCP separately from the already-known bfcache/unused-CSS shell issues. No action needed on the prerequisites box - it will appear automatically once testing/unit-testing-fundamentals lands on this integration branch.
